Document: Practice Direction – Civil Recovery Proceedings
Part 3 of 3
==================================================
## 13.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.3] An application under section 347 of the Act, or (where applicable) article 8 of the 2013 Order, for an order to grant entry may be made either –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.3] (1) together with an application for a production order; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.3] (2) by separate application, after a production order has been made. ## 13.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.4] An application notice for an order to grant entry must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.4] (1) specify the premises in relation to which the order is sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.4] (2) be supported by written evidence explaining why the order is needed. ## 13.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.5] A production order, or an order to grant entry, must contain a statement of the right of any person affected by the order to apply to vary or discharge the order. ## Search and seizure warrant

## 14.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.1] Omitted

## 14.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.2] The evidence in support of the application must state –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.2] (1) the matters relied on by the appropriate officer to show that one of the requirements in section 352(6) of the Act or, (where applicable) in article 13(4) of the 2013 Order, for the issue of a warrant is satisfied;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.2] (2) details of the premises to be subject to the warrant, and of the possible occupier or occupiers of those premises;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.2] (3) the name and position of the member of the staff of the appropriate officer who it is intended will execute the warrant. ## 14.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.3] There must be filed with the application notice drafts of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.3] (1) the warrant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.3] (2) a written undertaking by the person who is to execute the warrant to comply with paragraph 14.8 of this practice direction. ## 14.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] A search and seizure warrant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (1) specify the statutory power under which it is issued and, unless the court orders otherwise, give an indication of the nature of the investigation in respect of which it is issued;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (2) state the address or other identification of the premises to be subject to the warrant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (3) state the name of the member of the staff of the appropriate person who is authorised to execute the warrant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (4) set out the action which the warrant authorises the person executing it to take under the relevant sections of the Act or (where appropriate) the 2013 Order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (5) give the date on which the warrant is issued;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (6) include a statement that the warrant continues in force until the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which it is issued;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.4] (7) contain a statement of the right of any person affected by the order to apply to discharge or vary the order. ## 14.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.5] An example of a search and seizure warrant is annexed to this practice direction. This example may be modified as appropriate in any particular case. ## 14.6

## Rule 40.2 applies to a search and seizure warrant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > Rule 40.2 applies to a search and seizure warrant.] (CPR rule 40.2 requires every judgment or order to state the name and judicial title of the person making it, to bear the date on which it is given or made, and to be sealed by the court.)

## 14.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.7] Upon the issue of a warrant the court will provide to the appropriate officer –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.7] (1) the sealed warrant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.7] (2) a copy of it for service on the occupier or person in charge of the premises subject to the warrant. ## 14.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.8] A person attending premises to execute a warrant must, if the premises are occupied produce the warrant on arrival at the premises, and as soon as possible thereafter personally serve a copy of the warrant and an explanatory notice on the occupier or the person appearing to him to be in charge of the premises. ## 14.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 14.9] The person executing the warrant must also comply with any order which the court may make for service of any other documents relating to the application. ## Disclosure order

## 15.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.1] The application notice should normally name as respondents the persons on whom the appropriate officer intends to serve notices under the disclosure order sought. ## 15.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] A disclosure order must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] (1) give an indication of the nature of the investigation for the purposes of which the order is made;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] (2) set out the action which the order authorises the appropriate officer to take in accordance with section 357(4) of the Act or (where applicable) article 16(3) of the 2013 Order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] (3) contain a statement of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] (a) the offences relating to disclosure orders under section 359 of the Act or (where applicable) article 18 of the 2013 Order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.2] (b) the right of any person affected by the order to apply to discharge or vary the order. ## 15.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 15.3] Where, pursuant to a disclosure order, the appropriate officer gives to any person a notice under section 357(4) of the Act or (where applicable) article 16(3) of the 2013 Order, he must also at the same time serve on that person a copy of the disclosure order. ## Customer information order

## 16.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.1] The application notice should normally (unless it is impracticable to do so because they are too numerous) name as respondents the financial institution or institutions to which it is proposed that an order should apply. ## 16.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] A customer information order must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] (1) specify the financial institution, or description of financial institutions, to which it applies;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] (2) state the name of the person in relation to whom customer information is to be given, and any other details to identify that person;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] (3) contain a statement of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] (a) the offences relating to disclosure orders under section 366 of the Act or (where applicable) article 25 of the 2013 Order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.2] (b) the right of any person affected by the order to apply to discharge or vary the order. ## 16.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 16.3] Where, pursuant to a customer information order, the appropriate officer gives to a financial institution a notice to provide customer information, he must also at the same time serve a copy of the order on that institution. ## Account monitoring order

## 17.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.1] The application notice must name as a respondent the financial institution against which an account monitoring order is sought. ## 17.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] The application notice must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (1) state the matters required by section 370(2) and (3) of the Act or (where applicable) by article 29(2) and (3) of the 2013 Order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (2) give details of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (a) the person whose account or accounts the application relates to;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (b) each account or description of accounts in relation to which the order is sought, including if known the number of each account and the branch at which it is held;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (c) the information sought about the account or accounts;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (d) the period for which the order is sought;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.2] (e) the manner in which, and the frequency with which, it is proposed that the financial institution should provide account information during that period. ## 17.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 17.3] An account monitoring order must contain a statement of the right of any person affected by the order to apply to vary or discharge the order. ## Unexplained wealth order

## 18.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.1] (1) The application notice must name as a respondent the person who is required to be specified under section 362A(2)(b) of the Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.1] (2) In a case where the respondent is not an individual, the application notice may also name a person who is specified as a responsible officer of the respondent, pursuant to section 362(2A) of the Act. ## 18.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] The application notice must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (1) state the matters required by section 362A(2) and, if applicable, section 362A(2A) of the Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (2) specify what other information in connection with the property is sought (see section 362A(3)(d) of the Act) and what documents are sought (see section 362A(5));

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (3) specify whether the respondent is a politically exposed person in accordance with section 362B(4)(a) of the Act, or whether there are reasonable grounds to suspect that the respondent is, or has been, involved in serious crime in accordance with section 362B(4)(b) of the Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (4) give details of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (a) the nature of the Order sought in respect of the matters set out in section 362A(4) of the Act);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (b) the period within which compliance with the unexplained wealth order is sought (see section 362A(6) of the Act);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (c)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (i) the known sources of the respondent’s lawfully obtained income (see section 362B(3)(a) of the Act); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.2] (ii) the unlawful conduct through which it is suspected that the property has been obtained (see section 362B(3)(b) of the Act). ## 18.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] An unexplained wealth order must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] (1) state the person and the property to which it applies;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] (2) specify the matters set out in section 362A(3), including in particular what other information in connection with the property is to be provided (see section 362A(3)(d);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] (3) specify the matters set out in section 362A(4);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] (4) state the period within which the respondent or, if applicable, the specified responsible officer must comply with the order (see section 362A(6) of the Act);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.3] (5) contain a statement of the offences relating to unexplained wealth orders under section 362E of the Act. ## Interim freezing order

## 18.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.4] An application for an interim freezing order must be made –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.4] (1) to a High Court judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.4] (2) in accordance with section 362J(4) of the Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.4] (3) in accordance with CPR Part 23. ## 18.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.5] CPR rule 23.10(2), Sections I to V of CPR Part 25 do not apply to applications for interim freezing orders. ## 18.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.6] The application must be made without notice in the circumstances set out in section 362J(5) of the Act. ## 18.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.7] An application for an interim freezing order must be supported by written evidence which must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.7] (1) set out the grounds on which the order is sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.7] (2) give details of each item or description of property in respect of which the order is sought, including—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.7] (a)  the name of the respondent to the unexplained wealth order to which the interim freezing order relates; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.7] (b) an estimation of the value of the property. ## 18.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.8] CPR Part 69 (court’s power to appoint a receiver) and Practice Direction 69 apply to an application for the court to appoint a receiver under section 362N(2) of the Act with the following modifications—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.8] (1) paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 69 does not apply;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.8] (2) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must, in addition to the matters required by paragraph 4.1 of that practice direction, also identify a nominee and include the information in paragraph 4.2 of that practice direction. ## 18.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.9] An interim freezing order must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.9] (1) specify the matters required by section 362J(3) of the Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.9] (2) specify the period for which the prohibition referred to in that section will apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.9] (3) contain a statement of the right of any person affected by the order to apply to discharge or vary the order. ## 18.10

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10] The court shall have regard to the following when setting the period for which an interim freezing order has effect —

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10] (1) the period set under section 362A(6) for the respondent or, if applicable, the specified responsible officer to comply with the unexplained wealth order which applies to the property to which interim freezing order relates; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10] (2) the period allocated to the enforcement agency under section 362D(2) to (4)  to determine what enforcement or investigatory provisions it considers are to be taken in relation to the property(“the determination period”). ## Application to extend the determination period

## 18.10A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] An application under section 362DA of the Act to extend the determination period must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (a) be made to a High Court judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (b) be made in accordance with CPR Part 23; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (c) explain, pursuant to section 362DA—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (i) the work that the enforcement authority is undertaking towards making a determination under section 362D(2);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (ii) why further time is needed for the authority to make that determination; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (iii) why it is reasonable in all the circumstances for the period to be extended. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.10A] (Section 362DA of the Act specifies the limits which apply to an extension of the determination period.)

## Exclusions from interim freezing order for the purpose of meeting legal costs: general provisions

## 18.11

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.11] Subject to paragraph 18.12 when the court makes an interim freezing order on an application without notice, it will normally make an initial exclusion from the order for the purpose of enabling the respondent or, if applicable, the specified responsible officer to meet their reasonable legal costs so that they may—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.11] (1) take advice in relation to the order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.11] (2) prepare a statement of assets in accordance with paragraph 18.14; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.11] (3) if so advised, apply for the order to be varied or set aside. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.11] The total amount specified in the initial exclusion will not normally exceed £3,000. ## 18.12

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.12] To enable the court to consider whether it is appropriate to make or vary an exclusion, the court may order a party to file an estimate of costs. ## 18.13

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.13] The court will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs, other than an exclusion to meet the costs of taking any of the steps referred to in paragraph 18.11, unless that person has made, served and filed a statement of assets. ## 18.14

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.14] A statement of assets is a witness statement which sets out all the property which a person owns, holds or controls, or in which the person has an interest, giving the value, location and details of all such property. Information given in a statement of assets under this practice direction will be used only for the purpose of the civil recovery proceedings or in support of an application for an exclusion from a property freezing order or interim receiving order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs (see paragraph 7.3). ## 18.15

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.15] If the court is satisfied that a person has property to which the interim freezing order does not apply and from which the person may meet their or, if applicable, the specified responsible officer’s reasonable legal costs, it—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.15] (1) will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet those reasonable legal costs (including an initial exclusion under paragraph 18.11); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.15] (2) may set aside any exclusion which it has made for that purpose or reduce any amount specified in such an exclusion. ## 18.16

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.16] The court will normally refer to a costs judge any question relating to the amount which an exclusion should allow for reasonable legal costs in respect of proceedings under Chapter 2 of Part 8 of the Act. or a stage in those proceedings. ## 18.17

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.17] Attention is drawn to section 362L of the Act. An exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs must be made subject to the ‘required conditions’ specified in Part 2 of the Regulations. ## 18.18

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.18] An exclusion made for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs will specify—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.18] (1) the stage or stages in proceedings under Chapter 2 of Part 8 of the Act to which it relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.18] (2) the maximum amount which may be released in respect of legal costs for each specified stage; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.18] (3) the total amount which may be released in respect of legal costs pursuant to the exclusion. ## 18.19

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.19] A person should apply for a further exclusion or variation of an existing exclusion as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware that their legal costs—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.19] (1) in relation to any stage in proceedings under Chapter 2 of Part 8 of the Act have exceeded or will exceed the maximum amount specified in the exclusion for that stage; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 18.19] (2) in relation to all the stages to which the exclusion relates have exceeded or will exceed the total amount that may be released pursuant to the exclusion. ## ANNEX
